subject: math
title: Pythagoras' theorem: a² + b² = c² Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: For the 3-4-5 triangle, what is tan theta?
questions.feedback: If you picked 4/3, that is the trap: tan = adjacent / opposite. Reteach point: Always read TOA: tan is opposite over adjacent. So tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75, with the opposite side 3 on top and the adjacent side 4 underneath.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has legs 3 and 4. Find the hypotenuse and state the working.
questions.feedback: The working must square before adding: 9 + 16 = 25, then the square root gives c = 5. An answer of 7 means the lengths were added instead of the squares - that is the trap this lesson names.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has legs 6 and 8. What is its hypotenuse?
questions.feedback: Square and add: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, and the square root of 100 is 10. The choice 14 adds the lengths, and 100 forgets the final square root.

questions.prompt: In one or two sentences: how does the converse of Pythagoras' theorem let you test whether a triangle with sides 5, 12 and 13 is right-angled?
questions.answer: Check whether the two smaller squares add to the largest square: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13², so the triangle is right-angled, with the right angle opposite the side of length 13.
questions.feedback: A strong answer does the square check (25 + 144 = 169) instead of measuring angles. If the squares had not matched, the converse says the triangle cannot be right-angled.
